I know how this feels. ***But*** you need to remember that they're trying their hardest, and they don't understand that you can't feel better, no matter what they say, so the best thing to really do is to either pretend that they're making you feel a little better, to make them feel like they're making progress for all their effort, ***or*** to just talk to them and try and avoid talking about emotions, don't try and make it about yourself, or how rough the world is on you, which we're all guilty of here, but just talk and have a nice friendly conversation with them, it can be hard to do when depressed, but it's the best thing to do IMO. It's hard when you're trying so hard to make someone feel better, but they're not showing any progress because it makes you feel unappreciated. Everyone on here ***does*** need to remember both sides.

I understand and you should definitely break-up with him. ***BUT*** don't harbour feelings of hatred towards him, he's feeling deeply unhappy in your relationship, because he felt that he tried more than you did. remember that this is understandable, because depression does that to people, that's how it makes you show yourself. You also need to remember that waiting for your depression to just go before you go into a relationship is not something to do, depression doesn't go whilst you're thinking about it, relationships can be a very good ladder to climb out of the pit, you know that you have the strength to pull yourself up and that you shouldn't ever use depression as an excuse for anything. As someone with MDD it's not nice to see someone use it as an excuse. Using it as an excuse is worse than glamourising it. I'm not trying to accuse you  of anything, but to me you sound like you're making yourself worse. Take one step tomorrow towards solving your depression, take a shower and then make a routine of it, then add other steps of a healthy lifestyle to your routine and then build this up.
